headline: Seven Indonesian Airports Remain Shut as Anak Krakatau Disruption Hits 270,000 Travelers
seoTitle: Anak Krakatau: 7 Airports Shut, 270,000 Travelers Affected | FMB News
seoDescription: Seven Indonesian airports remained closed on September 7 as Anak Krakatau ash disrupted about 2,300 flights and more than 270,000 travelers, a major escalation from FMB News’ first report.
deck: The aviation disruption from Anak Krakatau has widened sharply: Reuters reports seven Indonesian airports remained closed, about 2,300 flights were affected and more than 270,000 travelers were impacted.
author: FMB News Desk

continuesFrom.headline: Anak Krakatau Eruption Disrupts Hundreds of Flights at Jakarta’s Main Airport
continuesFrom.whatChanged: FMB’s first report recorded 301 affected flights at Soekarno-Hatta. By September 7, Reuters reported seven Indonesian airports still closed, about 2,300 flights affected and more than 270,000 travelers impacted, making the disruption substantially broader and longer-lasting.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Seven Indonesian airports remained closed on September 7 because of volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau, extending a major aviation disruption that began over the weekend.

Reuters reported that more than 270,000 travelers had been affected and about 2,300 flights had been delayed, diverted or cancelled. The closures included Jakarta-area airports as authorities continued to assess ash conditions and aviation safety.
This is a developing story. FMB News will update this report as verified information becomes available.

sections.heading: What changed since FMB’s first report
paragraphs: FMB News’ September 6 report documented 301 affected flights at Soekarno-Hatta, including 58 international services. The September 7 figures show the event has expanded from a major Jakarta disruption into a wider, prolonged Indonesian aviation problem affecting multiple airports and hundreds of thousands of travelers.
The original September 6 article remains intact as the historical first report. This update is published separately because the scale and duration of the disruption are independently newsworthy.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Anak Krakatau lies in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra. Its current eruption sequence has sent ash high enough to disrupt aviation around western Indonesia, while schools in affected areas have shifted to remote learning and authorities continue monitoring public-health and transport impacts.

Volcanic ash is dangerous to aircraft because fine particles can damage engines and other systems. Airport reopening decisions therefore depend on ash concentration, wind movement and aviation-safety assessments rather than a fixed timetable.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Indonesia and Jakarta are major regional travel and business links for Filipinos. A disruption involving thousands of flights can affect direct travelers as well as passengers connecting through Singapore, Kuala Lumpur and other hubs when aircraft and crews are displaced across airline networks.

The larger scale also increases the chance of knock-on itinerary changes even for passengers whose specific flight has not yet been cancelled. Travelers should rely on airline and airport operational notices instead of assuming a scheduled departure will proceed unchanged.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The exact reopening time for every affected airport remains subject to volcanic ash and safety assessments.

The final number of disrupted flights and passengers may rise as airlines reconcile cancellations, diversions and rebookings. FMB News is not claiming a Philippine-carrier cancellation unless one is independently verified.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for Indonesian aviation notices on airport reopening, further Anak Krakatau eruptions, changes in ash-plume direction and updated airline schedules.
Filipino passengers traveling to or through Indonesia should check the operating airline’s official flight-status channel and any connection affected by Jakarta or other Indonesian airport closures.
